summary: Kunzang Namgyal studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrõl Lodrö Thaye.

Kunzang Pelden studied under Shenphen Nangwa, Patrul Rinpoche, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He taught Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Dodrupchen Rinpoche, Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, and Shechen Gyaltsab.

id: P:Kunzig Shamar Rinpoche Mipham Chokyi Lodro
summary: Kunzig Shamar Rinpoche Mipham Chokyi Lodro was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers the 16th Karmapa Rangjung Rigpe Dorje and Kalu Rinpoche (1973).

Kuo-Pin Chuang works in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning a Ph.D. from National Chung Hsing University. He was a postdoctoral fellow at National Taiwan University (2019–2022) and Edinburgh (2022), and is a professor at Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Kurt A. Behrendt specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, earning his PhD from UCLA in 1997. At the Metropolitan Museum of Art, he was Assistant Curator in Asian Art (~2006) and Associate Curator of South Asian Art (attested 2022).
Kurt Andrew Johnson studied Indology and earned his PhD from the University of York in 2010 under the supervision of Jane Moody.
Kurt Bruno Otto Fischer worked in Buddhist studies, studying under Paul Dahlke (~1924–1928). He succeeded Dahlke in 1928 and served as leader of Das Buddhistische Haus from ~1928 to 1942.

Kurt Friedrich Leidecker, a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religious studies, earned a B.A. from Oberlin and a Ph.D. from Chicago. He taught at Rensselaer, Lehigh, and Mary Washington (1948–1973), and directed the Thomas Jefferson Institute in 1974.

Kurt Huber, a scholar of philosophy, completed his PhD at the University of Munich (~1913–1917). He later served at the University of Munich as an außerordentlicher Professor in 1926 and held a professorship there in 1938.
Kurt Hutten specialized in religious studies and Indology. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Tübingen in 1930 under the doctoral supervision of Jakob Wilhelm Hauer.
Kurt Klemm, an Indologist and linguist, studied at Humboldt University of Berlin and earned his PhD at the University of Leipzig in 1894 under doctoral supervisors Ernst Windisch and Karl Brugmann.
Kurt Quecke was an Indologist who completed his Ph.D. at the University of Marburg in 1947 under the supervision of Johannes Nobel.
Kurt Schmidt, active in Buddhist studies, earned a Dr. iuris from the University of Rostock (~1897–1901) and founded the Buddhistische Arbeitsgemeinschaft in 1946.

Linguist Kurt Stegmann von Pritzwald completed his Ph.D. at the University of Jena (1928). He held posts at Jena, Kiel, and Rostock, and served as Lehrbeauftragte, Docent, and apl. Professor at the University of Marburg (1936–1945).

Kurt Tropper works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, earning a doctoral degree from the University of Vienna in 2001 under Ernst Steinkellner. He held posts as Vertragsassistent at the University of Vienna and at the Austrian Academy of Sciences.

Kurt Wulff, a scholar of linguistics and sinology, earned his M.A. and PhD from the University of Copenhagen. He worked at the Thesaurus Linguae Latinae and Royal Danish Library, then lectured and served as Docent at Copenhagen (1920–1928).
Kurt von Kamptz was an Indologist who studied under Walther Schubring and received his Ph.D. from the University of Hamburg (~1924–1929). He worked as a librarian at Wehrkreisbücherei IV Dresden.

Kurtis R. Schaeffer specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, earning an MA from Washington and a PhD from Harvard. He held faculty posts at the University of Alabama (2000–2004) and joined the University of Virginia in 2005.
Kurunegoda Piyatissa, who worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, served as the head of the New York Buddhist Vihara (attested 1998; also attested 2009).

Kwangsoo Park works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He earned an MA from the University of Iowa, a PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison, and served as a professor at Wonkwang University (attested 2020).
